title: Grace acting on the affections
source_text: XXVII. Deinde subjungunt mente illuminata, & voluntati concessa supernaturali potentia, partim per illuminationem, partim per virium immediatam infusionem, Deum quoque affectus nostros, & partem illam sensitivam corrigere, & bonis desideriis, quorum objecta monstrat intellectus, actus vero imperat voluntas, afficere; quibus affectibus magis, magisque correctis, castigatis, & in ordinem redactis, promptior & facilior, ac minus impedita postmodum redditur voluntas ad exercendos pietatis actus, non usque adeo, uti ante, reluctantibus affectibus, & lege illa in membris belligerante.
pass_a_gloss: XXVII. Then they subjoin that the mind having been illuminated, & supernatural power having been granted to the will, partly through illumination, partly through immediate infusion of strength, God also corrects our affections, & that sensitive part, & affects them with good desires, whose objects the intellect shows, but whose acts the will commands; which affections being more & more corrected, chastised, & reduced to order, the will is afterwards rendered more prompt & easy, and less hindered for exercising acts of piety, the affections not resisting so much, as before, & that law warring in the members.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXVII. They go on to say that once the mind has been enlightened and the will given supernatural power, partly by enlightening and partly by a direct infusion of strength, God also corrects our affections and that sensitive part of us. He moves them with good desires, whose objects the intellect points out and whose acts the will commands.

As those affections are corrected, disciplined and brought into order more and more, the will becomes readier, easier and less hindered in practising acts of devotion, since the affections and that law at war in our members no longer fight back as much as before.
